problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -5 \\ 2 & -2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 2 & -2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 4 & k-2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 0=k-10.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-10,$ which means that $k=10.$
